checks: The slice formulas give the exact moment inequality after the common unit-normal factor is removed. If the B trace is empty or a point, its length is zero and the base-only positive direction has derivative −t/‖u‖, agreeing with failure of inclusion of a length-t interval.

For a positive-length B support trace the moment theorem applies. If b<t both conditions fail. For b≥t the mass-t selector means range between the centers of the two end length-t intervals. Every center in between is realized by translating one interval, including the full-length case b=t. The prescribed mean equals the center of the stated J. Reflection through y exchanges the endpoint cutting lines, and c_K−y is tangent, so this is an equality of geometric containment conditions on the correct line.

The inclusion of the midpoint sum of E_A and F in E_K yields length at most s and exactly the claimed center tolerance. The midpoint sum with J instead has length t and center y−(s/(2t))(c_K−y); its containment gives (1+s/(2t))‖y−c_K‖≤(s−t)/2.

The length bounds give 0<t/s≤1. Exact symbolic replay verifies the completed-square identity and its zero at (√3−1)/2. The chord endpoint distances are s/2±‖y−c_K‖; evaluating their decreasing ratio at the stated maximum gives 1/√3. The attainment statement is only about the scalar maximum.
